narrativeReportMd:
# EvidenceVariable R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`EvidenceVariable` keeps the same resource identity in R6, but the local content model is substantially redesigned. The highest-impact break is the removal of the required R4 `characteristic` backbone, which every valid R4 instance had to carry, and its replacement by an optional R6 variable-definition/data-storage model. R4 instances using `type`, `jurisdiction`, `topic`, `subtitle`, or `relatedArtifact` also contain element names that are not present in the R6 resource.

## Scope
The assessment used the local R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions, package metadata, package indexes, manifest row, and selected local ValueSet/CodeSystem artifacts. Inherited base-resource changes are deliberately excluded and listed as out of scope.

## Main migration themes
The resource changed from a PICO-style characteristic list to a more granular variable model. R4 `characteristic.definition[x]` allowed direct references/canonicals and several choice datatypes; R6 instead uses `definition`, `definitionModifier`, `handling`, `category`, `conditional`, `dataStorage`, `timing`, `period`, `constraint`, and missing/unacceptable-data handling elements. This is not a simple rename because the cardinalities, element nesting, choice types, and terminology bindings all changed.

## Highest-impact findings
The required `EvidenceVariable.characteristic` removal is the clearest hard R4-to-R6 validation break. The `type` to `handling` change is the clearest terminology and code-generation break. The optional metadata/relationship-field removals are less universal but still hard breaks for instances that use those fields.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for deciding how to map R4 characteristics, `type`, `groupMeasure`, and related artifacts into the R6 model. The supplied inputs did not include an authoritative ConceptMap or migration guide.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Because R4 EvidenceVariable was trial-use/FMM 0 and R6 is marked normative/FMM 1 in the package, a redesign may be justified, but it was not backward compatible. A less disruptive path would have retained deprecated aliases or extensions for at least the required `characteristic` backbone and `type` code.

## Follow-up analysis
Cross-artifact review should check common MetadataResource/interface changes and base Resource/DomainResource differences separately. Terminology review should validate expansions and mappings for the R4 variable and group-measure codes versus R6 handling and definition-modifier concepts.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: EvidenceVariable has high-impact local breaking changes. The top migration concerns are: the required R4 `characteristic` backbone is removed; the primitive required-bound `type` code is replaced by a CodeableConcept-based `handling` model; and several optional R4 metadata/relationship fields are removed or reshaped. The main uncertainty is the absence of an authoritative R4-to-R6 ConceptMap or official migration narrative for the redesigned variable model.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is primarily a semantic remodeling exercise, not a field-by-field copy. R4 data centered on `characteristic.definition[x]`, optional exclusion/timing/aggregation fields, and a required `status`. R6 separates variable meaning, modifiers, handling, category, data storage, constraints, timing, and missing-data handling. R4-to-R6 transforms should therefore be rule-driven and reviewed by domain experts, especially when old instances use `definitionDataRequirement`, `definitionTriggerDefinition`, `definitionCanonical`, `exclude`, `groupMeasure`, or `relatedArtifact`.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for element presence, cardinality, type, local flag, and invariant findings because they are directly observable in the two StructureDefinitions. Confidence is medium for exact terminology and semantic migration impact because full terminology expansions, official diffs, and authoritative ConceptMaps were not available.

findings.title: Required R4 characteristic backbone was removed and replaced by a new variable model

affectedLocation.newPath: EvidenceVariable.definition / EvidenceVariable.definitionModifier / EvidenceVariable.dataStorage / EvidenceVariable.constraint and related R6 elements

oldState.summary: R4 required at least one EvidenceVariable.characteristic backbone element.

semanticText.short: What defines the members of the evidence element
semanticText.definition: A characteristic that defines the members of the evidence element. Multiple characteristics are applied with "and" semantics.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, a valid `EvidenceVariable` had to contain `characteristic` at least once. Each characteristic had a mandatory `definition[x]` and optional descriptive, usage-context, exclusion, participant-effective, time-from-start, and group-measure fields.

newState.summary: R6 has no EvidenceVariable.characteristic element; variable meaning and processing are represented by several optional top-level elements.

semanticText.definition: R6 introduces `definition`, `definitionModifier`, `handling`, `category`, `conditional`, `classifier`, `dataStorage`, `timing`, `period`, `constraint`, `missingDataMeaning`, and `unacceptableDataHandling` for variable semantics and data handling.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 distributes the former characteristic-centric concept across an optional root `definition`, modifier/value pairs, handling/category metadata, data-storage details, timing, and constraint elements. There is no direct element-name alias for R4 `characteristic`.

facts.note: Every valid R4 EvidenceVariable needed at least one characteristic.
No single R6 choice element preserves the full R4 choice domain.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old and new elements were matched by semantic role, not by id. R4 `characteristic` defined the evidence variable membership or criteria. R6 uses several differently shaped elements to represent variable meaning, qualification, data storage, timing, and constraints.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct R4-to-R6 validation break because `EvidenceVariable.characteristic` is not present in R6, while R4 required it. Strict R6 validators and generated R6 parsers should reject or ignore the old element depending on parser policy. It is also a high R6-to-R4 conversion risk because R6 instances can express variable semantics in multiple new optional fields that do not collapse losslessly into the old required characteristic backbone.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: EvidenceVariable encodes evidence-analysis semantics; a lossy or incorrect transform could change the population, exposure, outcome, timing, or data-quality interpretation of an evidence variable.

justification.inferredGoal: Modernize EvidenceVariable from a PICO characteristic model into a richer variable definition and data-handling model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `characteristic` as an optional legacy backbone while adding the new R6 variable-definition and data-handling elements.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of replacing the R4 PICO characteristic backbone with a richer variable-definition, timing, constraint, and data-handling model is reasonable. The breaking removal is not strictly unavoidable, but the compatibility alternative would keep two overlapping models for the core meaning of the resource, so the level of breakage is probably justified for a substantial redesign.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could have left `EvidenceVariable.characteristic` in place as a deprecated `0..*` legacy backbone and added the new R6 elements beside it. That would accept most R4 instances unchanged. The alternative is only partial because R6 instances could then express the same variable through both `characteristic` and the new fields, requiring precedence, consistency rules, and migration pressure that might never eliminate the old representation.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old wire compatibility but creates duplicate same-resource representations for variable meaning, with conflict and indefinite-legacy-use risk.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `EvidenceVariable.characteristic` as a local BackboneElement with cardinality 1..*.
R4 requires `characteristic.definition[x]` with Reference(Group), canonical(ActivityDefinition), CodeableConcept, Expression, DataRequirement, and TriggerDefinition choices.
No R6 element has id `EvidenceVariable.characteristic`; R6 instead defines `definition`, `definitionModifier`, `handling`, `category`, `dataStorage`, `constraint`, and related fields.
R6 `definition` is optional and uses CodeableReference(Group).

examples.examplesMd: The R4 example is intentionally small but illustrates the mandatory old backbone. The R6 example shows new variable semantics and data-storage content that has no single R4 element equivalent.

findings.narrativeMd: `EvidenceVariable.characteristic` was the core of the R4 resource and was mandatory. R6 removes that backbone entirely and uses a different set of optional elements to represent what the variable means, how it is measured, where its data is stored, and how values are constrained or interpreted. This is the primary breaking change for R4 data and R4-generated models.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid instance containing the required `characteristic` element can become R6-invalid because the element is not defined in R6. Conversely, an R6 instance using `definition`, `definitionModifier`, `dataStorage`, or `constraint` cannot be represented in R4 without constructing a synthetic `characteristic` and often losing details. The validation mechanism is ordinary FHIR element-name and cardinality validation, plus choice-type validation for the old `definition[x]` and new replacement fields.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not treat this as a simple rename. Build a mapping policy that classifies each R4 `characteristic` as variable definition, modifier, category, timing, constraint, data-storage, or missing/unacceptable-data handling. Test old instances using each R4 `definition[x]` choice, `exclude`, `participantEffective[x]`, `timeFromStart`, and `groupMeasure`. Where no safe mapping exists, preserve the original content in an extension and require manual review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible alternative was partially available: keep `characteristic` as optional/deprecated and add the new R6 fields. That would have preserved wire compatibility for R4 instances but at the cost of duplicated semantics and possible conflicts between old and new representations. Because the R4 resource was low maturity, the redesign may be acceptable, but it remains materially breaking for implementers.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: This finding intentionally groups several removed R4 subelements because they were all nested under the mandatory old backbone and participate in the same model redesign. A separate migration guide or ConceptMap would improve confidence in exact element-to-element mappings.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 required at least one `EvidenceVariable.characteristic`, with a required `characteristic.definition[x]`; R6 removes that backbone and spreads variable meaning, timing, constraints, storage, and missing-data handling across new optional top-level elements. That is a genuine old-valid/new-invalid break for essentially every valid R4 EvidenceVariable and migration can require domain judgment, especially for DataRequirement, TriggerDefinition, exclusion, timing, and aggregation content. The break nevertheless appears proportionate because the R6 model is a substantial redesign rather than a simple rename, and keeping the old backbone beside the new model would leave two competing ways to express the core variable.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `EvidenceVariable.characteristic` is 1..* BackboneElement and `characteristic.definition[x]` is 1..1 with Reference(Group), canonical(ActivityDefinition), CodeableConcept, Expression, DataRequirement, and TriggerDefinition choices.

R6 StructureDefinition: no `EvidenceVariable.characteristic`; replacements include `definition`, `definitionModifier`, `dataStorage`, `timing`, `period`, `constraint`, `missingDataMeaning`, and `unacceptableDataHandling`.

HL7 EBMonFHIR IG v1.0.0-ballot says the evidence-related resources, including EvidenceVariable, are first ready for use in FHIR R5, with R6 enhancements; quick checks found specialized EBM use but not broad R4 production exchange evidence.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 0 and trial-use status substantially soften the stability expectation. The path was central and required, so the break is real, but low maturity and the official EBM IG's R5/R6 emphasis make broad R4 production impact less certain.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 instance containing the required `characteristic` element has an element not defined in R6; R6-to-R4 loss is also possible because new R6 variable-detail fields do not collapse cleanly into one R4 characteristic.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking R6 base could have kept `characteristic` as a deprecated legacy backbone while adding the new elements. That would preserve old wire instances, but it is not low cost: it creates duplicate core representations, conflict/precedence questions, and long-term pressure to support the R4 PICO-shaped model indefinitely.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high-impact hard-break assessment, but the fresh FMM-informed judgment weighs the low R4 maturity and redesign tradeoff more heavily; agree that the less-breaking alternative is only partial.

findings.title: R4 type code was removed and replaced by R6 handling CodeableConcept

oldState.summary: R4 had optional primitive `type` code with a required binding to variable-type.

binding.description: Codes include dichotomous, continuous, and descriptive.

oldState.narrativeMd: `EvidenceVariable.type` was a primitive code, so generated R4 models commonly expose it as a string or enum constrained by the required R4 value set.

newState.summary: R6 has no `type`; the closest element is optional `handling` as CodeableConcept with an example binding.

binding.description: Example codes include boolean, continuous, dichotomous, ordinal, polychotomous, time-to-event, and not-specified.

newState.narrativeMd: `EvidenceVariable.handling` is a complex CodeableConcept and its example binding is not validation-equivalent to the old required primitive-code binding.

facts.note: The R6 list is from the local example CodeSystem; the binding is not required.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element names differ, but the R6 `handling` short description and value set cover the same statistical-handling space as the R4 `type` codes more closely than any other R6 element.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 instance containing `type` has an unknown element in R6. Generated code also changes from a primitive code/enum to a complex CodeableConcept. R6 instances can carry multiple codings or text and can use example-binding concepts with no R4 required-code equivalent, so down-conversion needs terminology mapping or may be lossy.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The value describes statistical handling. Incorrect mapping can affect analysis logic even if it does not directly identify a patient.

justification.inferredGoal: Replace a narrow primitive enum with a more expressive statistical-handling concept.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep deprecated primitive `type` alongside the new `handling` CodeableConcept and define consistency rules when both are populated.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving from a narrow required-bound primitive code to a CodeableConcept with a broader handling vocabulary is a reasonable R6 modeling goal. Retaining the old optional `type` element would have reduced breakage, but it would also create duplicate ways to state statistical handling and require mapping or invariants to avoid inconsistent values.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have added `handling` while preserving `type` as a deprecated legacy element. This would keep R4 instances with `type` valid in R6. It is a partial alternative because old and new values do not have a complete one-to-one code relationship and duplicate same-resource representations could diverge or persist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids old-instance rejection but leaves two overlapping statistical-handling fields, possible conflicts, and extra implementation burden.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `type` as `code`, 0..1, isSummary true, with required binding to `ValueSet/variable-type|4.0.1`.
The local R4 CodeSystem includes `dichotomous`, `continuous`, and `descriptive`.
R6 defines `handling` as `CodeableConcept`, 0..1, with example binding to `ValueSet/variable-handling-example`.
The local R6 example CodeSystem includes `boolean`, `continuous`, `dichotomous`, `ordinal`, `polychotomous`, `time-to-event`, and `not-specified`.

examples.examplesMd: The `continuous` mapping is likely straightforward. `descriptive` and new R6 codes such as `time-to-event` require policy decisions because the local code sets are not identical and the binding strength changed.

findings.narrativeMd: `EvidenceVariable.type` is gone in R6. The closest replacement is `handling`, but it is not wire-compatible: it changes the property name, datatype, binding strength, and code set. This affects validators, generated classes, enum switches, search/index logic that assumed a primitive field, and analytics code that interpreted R4 variable types.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 content with `type` is old-valid/new-invalid under strict R6 validation because `type` is not an R6 element. R6 `handling` content is not cleanly R4-representable when it uses multiple codings, text-only concepts, or codes outside the old required `variable-type` set. The old and new value sets overlap for `continuous` and `dichotomous`, but not for every code inspected locally.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create an explicit mapping table. Map `continuous` and `dichotomous` to equivalent R6 handling codings where appropriate; decide how to map or preserve R4 `descriptive`; and decide whether R6 `boolean`, `ordinal`, `polychotomous`, `time-to-event`, and `not-specified` can down-convert to R4 or require extensions. Update codegen models from primitive enum handling to CodeableConcept handling.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This could have been less disruptive by retaining `type` as a deprecated field or by adding `handling` as an optional supplement. That would have preserved old instances but left two partly overlapping ways to classify handling. A ConceptMap would mitigate the break, but no authoritative one was supplied.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The binding comparison used local CodeSystem concepts where available; full value set expansion was not performed.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `EvidenceVariable.type` was an optional primitive `code` with a required binding to `variable-type`; R6 removes it and uses optional `handling` as a `CodeableConcept` with an example binding. Old instances that populated `type` need a wire-name and datatype migration, and generated APIs may move from an enum/string to a complex concept. The modeling goal is reasonable because statistical handling is more expressive in R6 and the old code set was narrow.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `EvidenceVariable.type` is 0..1 `code`, isSummary true, required binding `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/variable-type|4.0.1`.
R4 local CodeSystem `variable-type` contains `dichotomous`, `continuous`, and `descriptive`.
R6 StructureDefinition: closest replacement `EvidenceVariable.handling` is 0..1 `CodeableConcept`, example binding `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/variable-handling-example`.
R6 local handling codes include `boolean`, `continuous`, `dichotomous`, `ordinal`, `polychotomous`, `time-to-event`, and `not-specified`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 0/trial-use reduces the burden to preserve this optional enum exactly. The field can affect analysis semantics, but there was no quick evidence of broad R4 production exchange depending on the old primitive shape.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid and runtime/API/codegen: populated R4 `type` is not an R6 element, and generated code changes from primitive required-bound code to CodeableConcept. R6-to-R4 conversion can be lossy for new handling codes or multi-coding concepts.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained deprecated `type` alongside `handling`, or made a transitional alias. That preserves old instances, but it creates overlapping statistical-handling fields and requires consistency rules where old and new values disagree or lack one-to-one terminology mappings.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing hard-break and high runtime-risk mechanism, but the fresh judgment treats the optionality, low FMM, and reasonable R6 expressivity goal as making the break probably acceptable.

findings.title: Several optional R4 metadata and relationship fields were removed or reshaped

affectedLocation.newPath: EvidenceVariable.relatesTo and other R6 metadata additions

oldState.summary: R4 locally defined optional `subtitle`, `jurisdiction`, `topic`, and `relatedArtifact` elements.
oldState.narrativeMd: `jurisdiction` and `topic` supported metadata classification. `relatedArtifact` used the RelatedArtifact datatype for citations, dependencies, and documentation. `subtitle` carried an explanatory or alternate title.

newState.summary: R6 has no local `subtitle`, `jurisdiction`, `topic`, or `relatedArtifact` elements; it adds `relatesTo` and other administrative fields instead.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 introduces `relatesTo` as a local BackboneElement with mandatory `type` and `target[x]` inside each relationship, and adds fields such as `citeAs`, `recorder`, `purpose`, and `copyrightLabel`. These are not JSON-compatible replacements for the removed R4 fields.

facts.newValue: EvidenceVariable.relatesTo: BackboneElement 0..* with type 1..1 and target[x] 1..1

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `relatedArtifact` and `relatesTo` are semantically related because both express relationships to artifacts/resources, but the content model is different. `jurisdiction`, `topic`, and `subtitle` have no direct R6 local element with the same name.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The removed fields are optional, so not every R4 instance is affected. However, any R4 instance using them contains element names that are not valid in R6. Relationship data also needs structural conversion because R6 `relatesTo` is not the R4 RelatedArtifact datatype.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The main risk is loss of provenance, citation, jurisdiction, and discovery metadata rather than direct clinical data corruption.

justification.inferredGoal: Align EvidenceVariable metadata and relationships with a newer knowledge-artifact metadata pattern.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the removed optional metadata fields as deprecated base elements while adding `relatesTo` and the revised R6 metadata pattern.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Aligning EvidenceVariable with a newer metadata and relationship pattern is plausible, but the removed R4 fields were optional and the local evidence does not show that retaining them would have blocked the R6 goal. The breakage is therefore not clearly justified, especially for `subtitle`, `jurisdiction`, and `topic`; `relatedArtifact` has a stronger tradeoff because it overlaps with `relatesTo`.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could have kept `subtitle`, `jurisdiction`, `topic`, and `relatedArtifact` as deprecated elements while introducing `relatesTo` and other R6 metadata fields. This would preserve R4 instances that used those optional fields. The alternative is partial because `relatedArtifact` and `relatesTo` are competing relationship models, and duplicated metadata could create ambiguity about which representation is authoritative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve many old instances, but duplicates relationship and metadata paths and requires precedence and mapping rules.

evidence.detail: R4 defines optional `jurisdiction` as CodeableConcept 0..* with extensible jurisdiction binding.
R4 defines optional `topic` as CodeableConcept 0..* with example definition-topic binding.
R4 defines optional `relatedArtifact` as RelatedArtifact 0..*.
R6 has no local `subtitle`, `jurisdiction`, `topic`, or `relatedArtifact` elements and defines `relatesTo` instead.
Each R6 `relatesTo` backbone item requires a `type` and a `target[x]`.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example illustrates one possible `relatedArtifact.citation` to `relatesTo.targetMarkdown` transform, but exact mapping depends on the old RelatedArtifact fields used and the desired R6 relationship code.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 EvidenceVariable included several optional metadata and relationship elements that are absent in R6. These are not inherited base-resource fields in this StructureDefinition; they are local resource elements. Systems that stored jurisdiction/topic metadata or related artifacts directly on EvidenceVariable must move, drop, or extend that content.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances using any removed field become R6-invalid under strict element validation. R6 `relatesTo` content may not be exactly R4-representable because its target choice includes `uri`, `Attachment`, `canonical(Resource)`, `Reference(Resource)`, and `markdown`, while R4 used the RelatedArtifact datatype with its own fields and semantics.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory old instances for `subtitle`, `jurisdiction`, `topic`, and `relatedArtifact`. For `relatedArtifact`, define a case-by-case mapping into `relatesTo.type` and `target[x]`; preserve unsupported fields in extensions. For `jurisdiction`, `topic`, and `subtitle`, decide whether to use extensions, an ImplementationGuide-specific profile, or external catalog metadata.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because these fields were optional, preserving them as deprecated fields would have been technically possible and would have avoided strict validation breaks for existing instances. The tradeoff is that R6 would need rules for duplication with the new metadata model.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Search parameters were not assessed, but the package indexes suggest corresponding discovery/search behavior may also need separate review.

freshReview.narrativeMd: This finding groups several optional R4 metadata and relationship elements: `subtitle`, `jurisdiction`, `topic`, and `relatedArtifact`. R6 removes those wire names and introduces `relatesTo` for relationships, but `subtitle`, `jurisdiction`, and `topic` do not have direct same-name replacements. Because these fields are optional, the prevalence may be limited; however, if present they become strict R6 validation breaks and can carry discovery, jurisdiction, classification, or citation context. Retaining at least the non-overlapping metadata fields as deprecated base elements looks like a modest-cost compatibility design that would not obviously block the R6 model.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `subtitle` 0..1 string, `jurisdiction` 0..* CodeableConcept, `topic` 0..* CodeableConcept, and `relatedArtifact` 0..* RelatedArtifact.
R6 StructureDefinition: no local `subtitle`, `jurisdiction`, `topic`, or `relatedArtifact` elements were found.
R6 StructureDefinition: `relatesTo` is 0..* BackboneElement with required `type` CodeableConcept and required `target[x]` choice.
R4 package includes EvidenceVariable search parameters for jurisdiction, topic, and relationship-style metadata, showing these fields were exposed as discovery surfaces in R4 core.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 0/trial-use softens assumptions about widespread deployed content, but these are ordinary metadata and relationship paths that are plausible in cataloged evidence artifacts. The low maturity does not fully justify removing optional discovery/citation fields when cheap transitional retention appears possible.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances using any removed field have undefined R6 elements. There is also metadata/tooling impact for catalog, search, and citation workflows that used jurisdiction, topic, subtitle, or RelatedArtifact.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking R6 base could have retained `subtitle`, `jurisdiction`, and `topic` as deprecated optional metadata and either retained `relatedArtifact` transiently or provided a more explicit compatibility rule to `relatesTo`. The tradeoff is real for `relatedArtifact` because it overlaps with `relatesTo`, but the other optional metadata paths appear cheaper to preserve.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing medium-impact assessment and partial alternative finding, but the fresh review is more action-oriented: the grouped removal deserves revisit because several optional metadata fields seem preservable at low cost.

findings.title: status changed from mandatory in R4 to optional in R6

oldState.narrativeMd: `EvidenceVariable.status` was mandatory and modifier-marked in R4. R4 instances without it were invalid.

newState.summary: R6 makes status optional with meaningWhenMissing = Value is unknown.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the status element as a modifier and summary element, but permits it to be absent and defines missing status as unknown.

facts.note: Local CodeSystem concept list was unchanged.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 validation break because all R4 instances already have `status` and those values remain in the local PublicationStatus code set. It is a hard R6-to-R4 representability issue: an R6 instance may omit a modifier element that R4 required, and a converter must choose or infer a status such as `unknown` to produce valid R4.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Status is modifier-marked because retired artifacts require special handling. Treating missing R6 status incorrectly as active could affect governance and use decisions.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow unknown lifecycle status to be represented by omission rather than requiring an explicit code.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable: R4 instances already include `status` and remain R6-compatible for this element; the risk is R6-to-R4 down-conversion when R6 omits it.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 change loosens cardinality and defines missing status as unknown, which is coherent with the existing `unknown` publication-status code. Because this does not make R4-valid instances invalid in R6, the backward-compatible-alternative question for R4-to-R6 base design is not applicable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed for this finding: R4 resources with the required `status` can be copied forward. Keeping `status` mandatory would be a down-conversion-friendly design choice, not a backward-compatible alternative under this calibration.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeping `status` required would ease down-conversion but would force R6 authors to send explicit `unknown` instead of relying on `meaningWhenMissing`.

evidence.detail: R4 status has min 1, max 1, isModifier true, and required PublicationStatus binding.
R6 status has min 0, max 1, isModifier true, required PublicationStatus binding, and meaningWhenMissing.
The local PublicationStatus concept list remains draft, active, retired, unknown in both inspected packages.

examples.examplesMd: An R6 instance with omitted status is not directly valid R4. The migration example shows the safest generic backfill when no lifecycle state is known.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 loosens `EvidenceVariable.status` from mandatory to optional. That helps R6 authors but creates a reverse-direction break because R4 requires a status and treats it as a modifier. The code set itself did not materially change in the local CodeSystem files inspected.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation is not broken by this cardinality change. R6-to-R4 validation is broken for R6 instances with no `status`; an R4 validator will reject them unless a value is supplied. Runtime code that assumed status is always present must now handle absence in R6.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R4-to-R6, copy `status` as-is. For R6-to-R4, populate `unknown` only when no reliable lifecycle status is available; otherwise preserve the actual status. Test application logic that filters out retired or inactive artifacts so missing R6 status is not accidentally treated as active.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 change could have preserved R4 compatibility by keeping `status` required and using the existing `unknown` code for unknown status. The chosen design is more permissive but shifts responsibility to validators and converters.

freshReview.narrativeMd: This is a cardinality loosening, not an R4-to-R6 instance break. Every valid R4 EvidenceVariable already has `status`, and the same publication-status codes remain available in R6. R6 authors may omit status, which creates a down-conversion concern, but R6 also gives missing status the meaning of unknown, and R4 has an `unknown` code that can represent that case.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `EvidenceVariable.status` is 1..1 `code`, modifier, summary, with required PublicationStatus binding.
R6 StructureDefinition: `EvidenceVariable.status` is 0..1 `code`, modifier, summary, with required PublicationStatus binding.
Local PublicationStatus concepts remain `draft`, `active`, `retired`, and `unknown` in the inspected packages.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 0/trial-use further lowers concern, but the main reason for the judgment is that R4-to-R6 compatibility is widened for this path.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: an R6 instance with omitted status needs a value for R4, but `unknown` is an available and semantically aligned fallback. No old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 mechanism was found.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping `status` mandatory in R6 would ease down-conversion, but it is not needed to preserve R4 instances moving forward. The R6 omission design is a permissive base-model choice rather than a backward-compatibility failure.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with treating this as medium practical impact for R4-to-R6 migration; agree only that there is a reverse-direction representability consideration.

findings.title: effectivePeriod was removed from the R6 summary view

oldState.summary: R4 effectivePeriod was included in summaries.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 marked `effectivePeriod` with `isSummary: true`, so summary-oriented serializers and REST `_summary` responses could include it.

newState.summary: R6 effectivePeriod remains optional Period but is no longer a summary element.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 keeps the element name, type, and cardinality but changes summary inclusion behavior.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This does not affect full-instance validation or JSON element representation. It can affect clients that rely on summary responses, generated summary projections, indexing, or UI cards that expected `effectivePeriod` in compact representations.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The main risk is missing applicability-period context in summary displays or lightweight synchronization flows.

justification.inferredGoal: Reduce summary payload size or align summary elements with a revised metadata pattern.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `effectivePeriod` marked `isSummary: true` and let clients or servers use explicit element selection when they need smaller projections.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Removing `effectivePeriod` from the summary view is not a full-instance validation break, but it can affect clients that rely on summary responses. The local definitions show the flag change but not a reason that summary compatibility had to be broken, and preserving the flag would have had a modest long-term cost.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backward-compatible base design could simply have retained `isSummary: true` for `effectivePeriod`. Systems that wanted leaner projections could still request explicit elements or use implementation-specific summary behavior. This preserves R4 summary expectations with little semantic downside.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Low tradeoff: preserves summary clients at the cost of a slightly larger or less-curated default summary view.

evidence.detail: R4 has `isSummary: true` for `effectivePeriod`.
R6 has `isSummary: false` for `effectivePeriod`.

examples.examplesMd: No instance fragment is needed because the wire element is unchanged in full representations; the effect appears in summary serialization and generated summary views.

findings.narrativeMd: `EvidenceVariable.effectivePeriod` still exists in R6, but it drops out of summary mode. This is a runtime/API-shape issue rather than a validation break.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Full R4 and R6 instances with `effectivePeriod` remain structurally compatible for this element. The compatibility risk is that clients using FHIR summary behavior may no longer receive the field in R6 summary responses and must request full resources or specific elements.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit consumers that use `_summary=true`, summary projections, generated lightweight DTOs, or search-result cards for EvidenceVariable. If they need applicability dates, request full resources or explicitly include `effectivePeriod` where the server supports element selection.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The backward-compatible alternative was simply to preserve `isSummary: true`. Since this is not a full-instance validation break, the compatibility cost is lower than the content-model removals, but clients relying on summaries still need attention.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `effectivePeriod` keeps the same name, type, and cardinality, but R6 no longer marks it as a summary element. Full-resource instances remain compatible; the risk is limited to summary projections, REST `_summary` behavior, generated lightweight DTOs, or UI cards that expected applicability timing in compact representations. That is a real API/projection change, but it is narrow and can usually be handled by requesting the full resource or explicit elements.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition: `EvidenceVariable.effectivePeriod` is 0..1 Period with `isSummary: true`.
R6 StructureDefinition: `EvidenceVariable.effectivePeriod` remains 0..1 Period but has `isSummary: false`.
No quick evidence was found that R4 EvidenceVariable summary responses are a broad production exchange dependency.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 0/trial-use softens the concern for summary-view compatibility. The element can be useful for applicability timing, but the affected surface is summary output rather than full instance validity.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen: summary-only responses or generated summary projections may omit `effectivePeriod` in R6. Full-instance validation and serialization are unchanged for this element.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping `isSummary: true` would have been the least-breaking base design and has low apparent cost beyond a slightly larger or less curated summary view. Still, because the break is summary-only and low-FMM, it does not rise to a revisit-level concern without evidence of deployed reliance.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing low runtime-impact finding and the existence of a simple alternative, but disagree that the simple alternative makes this a material standards concern under the FMM-informed framework.

findings.title: Local warning constraints for name and URL changed

oldState.summary: R4 had root warning `evv-0` for machine-usable names and no local URL warning.

constraints.human: Name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation

oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 name warning used an EvidenceVariable-specific key and allowed a one-character name by expression shape.

newState.summary: R6 replaces the name warning with `cnl-0` and adds URL warning `cnl-1`.

constraints.human: Name should be usable as an identifier for the module by machine processing applications such as code generation
URL should not contain | or # - these characters make processing canonical references problematic

newState.narrativeMd: The R6 name warning is explicitly conditional on name existing, uses a new key, anchors the pattern, and requires at least one character after the leading capital. R6 also warns when canonical URL values contain `|`, `#`, or space.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Both constraints are warnings, so they should not make instances invalid in normal validation. They can still affect QA gates that fail on warnings, generated-code naming checks, canonical URL quality checks, or tools that key behavior by invariant id.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The URL warning protects canonical-reference processing; the name warning protects code generation and machine processing.

justification.inferredGoal: Standardize canonical/name warning constraints and detect canonical URLs that are difficult to process.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the old `evv-0` name warning as a deprecated alias while adding standardized `cnl-0` and URL warning `cnl-1`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Standardizing canonical/name warnings and flagging URL characters that interfere with canonical-reference processing are reasonable goals, and the constraints remain warnings rather than hard validation errors. A compatibility alias for the old invariant key would help some tooling, but it would not eliminate the new warning behavior and would add duplicate warning management.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would keep `evv-0` in the StructureDefinition as a deprecated warning alias while adding `cnl-0` and `cnl-1`. This is only a partial alternative because warning-as-error pipelines could still fail on the new URL or stricter name warnings, and duplicate invariant keys can confuse validators, dashboards, and QA baselines.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Alias preservation helps key-based tooling but duplicates warnings and does not avoid new warning-sensitive impacts from the stricter name and URL checks.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `evv-0` as a warning on `name`.
R6 defines `cnl-0` as a warning with a revised name expression.
R6 adds `cnl-1` warning that URL should not contain pipe, hash, or space.

examples.examplesMd: The example is not R6-invalid solely because of these constraints; the new constraints are warnings. It illustrates values that can pass old warning policy but trigger R6 warning policy.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 tightens and standardizes local conformance warnings. The name invariant changes key and expression, and a new URL warning flags characters that make canonical-reference processing problematic. This is not a hard validation break, but it matters for warning-sensitive pipelines and code generation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Because both R6 constraints are warnings, ordinary FHIR validation should still accept affected instances unless a local policy treats warnings as failures. Tooling that records invariant keys may see `evv-0` disappear and `cnl-0`/`cnl-1` appear.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update QA baselines and code-generation checks to use `cnl-0` and `cnl-1`. Review canonical URLs containing `|`, `#`, or spaces and consider normalizing them before migration. If one-character names are intentionally used, decide whether local warning policy should tolerate them.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The new URL warning is a reasonable addition, and keeping severity at warning is a compatibility-preserving choice. The invariant key change could have been documented or aliased for tools that depend on stable keys.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The changed name and URL constraints are warning-level quality checks. R6 standardizes the name warning key/expression and adds a warning for canonical URLs containing characters that complicate canonical-reference processing. These warnings can affect strict QA baselines that fail on warnings, but they do not make ordinary instances invalid and the new URL warning is a reasonable interoperability safeguard.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition root warning `evv-0`: `name.matches('[A-Z]([A-Za-z0-9_]){0,254}')`.
R6 StructureDefinition root warning `cnl-0`: `name.exists() implies name.matches('^[A-Z]([A-Za-z0-9_]){1,254}$')`.
R6 StructureDefinition URL warning `cnl-1`: `exists() implies matches('^[^|# ]+$')`.
All inspected constraints in this finding have severity `warning`, not `error`.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 0/trial-use further reduces stability concern for warning-key and QA-baseline churn. The warning nature is the main driver of the no-problem judgment.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: warning-level: warning-as-error pipelines or invariant-key dashboards may need updates, but ordinary structural validation is not an old-valid/new-invalid break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept `evv-0` as a deprecated alias, but that would duplicate warnings and still would not avoid the new URL warning. Since the checks remain warnings, an alias is not a compelling base-model alternative.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: mostly agree with the existing low-impact assessment, but the fresh judgment treats the partial alias alternative as unnecessary rather than a reason for concern.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The R6 StructureDefinition is present and keeps the same canonical URL, id, name, type, kind, baseDefinition, derivation, and abstract flag. No rename, split, merge, or removal was detected.

Among local EvidenceVariable elements compared, `status` remains modifier-marked and no local non-base element gained or lost modifier status. Inherited `implicitRules` and `modifierExtension` are out of scope.
No local EvidenceVariable ElementDefinition fixed value, pattern value, or default value constraints were found in the compared snapshots.
No local slicing definitions or slice identities were found for EvidenceVariable in either snapshot.

The local PublicationStatus CodeSystem concepts were checked and remained `draft`, `active`, `retired`, and `unknown`. Material binding changes for `type`/`handling`, removed `groupMeasure`, and new R6 example bindings are reported separately. Full terminology-server expansions were not performed.

No additional reference-target narrowing was found among unchanged local element names. Major reference/choice-domain changes are part of the `characteristic` removal and `relatesTo`/new-model findings.

The resourceType remains `EvidenceVariable`; no artifact-level JSON/XML identity change was found. Serialization risk comes from removed, renamed, and reshaped local elements documented in findings, not from a resourceType rename.
